title_en: Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Consumer Civil Public Interest Litigation Cases

articles.content_en:
This Interpretation shall apply to consumer civil public interest lawsuits initiated by the China Consumers' Association and the consumers' associations established in provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government against operators for acts that infringe upon the lawful rights and interests of numerous unspecified consumers, or that endanger the personal or property safety of consumers, or otherwise harm the public interest.
This Interpretation shall apply to consumer civil public interest lawsuits initiated by organs or social organizations as provided by law or authorized by the National People's Congress or its Standing Committee.

The jurisdiction over consumer civil public interest lawsuit cases shall be governed by the relevant provisions of Article 285 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.
With the approval of the Supreme People's Court, a Higher People's Court may, based on the actual circumstances of its jurisdiction, designate certain Intermediate People's Courts within its jurisdiction to accept first-instance consumer civil public interest lawsuit cases.

Where the People's Court considers that the claims made by the plaintiff are insufficient to protect the public interest, it may explain to the plaintiff and suggest that the plaintiff modify or add claims such as cessation of infringement.

After accepting a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case, the People's Court shall publish a notice of the acceptance and, within ten days from the date of docketing, notify the relevant administrative department in writing.

After accepting a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case, if other organs or social organizations that may initiate a lawsuit according to law apply to participate in the lawsuit before the first-instance trial, the People's Court may permit their participation.
If the People's Court permits participation, they shall be listed as co-plaintiffs; if the application is made after the time limit, it shall not be permitted.
An organ or social organization entitled to initiate a consumer civil public interest lawsuit may apply for preservation of evidence in accordance with Article 81 of the Civil Procedure Law.

After accepting a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case, if consumers who have suffered damage from the same tortious act apply to participate in the lawsuit, the People's Court shall inform them to assert their rights in accordance with Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law.

After a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case is accepted, if consumers who have suffered damage from the same tortious act request to suspend the lawsuit initiated by them under Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court may permit such suspension.
During the trial of a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case, if the defendant files a counterclaim, the People's Court shall not accept it.
If the plaintiff admits facts unfavorable to itself during the proceedings, and the People's Court considers that doing so would harm the public interest, such admission shall not be confirmed.

In a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case, if the plaintiff requests the defendant to bear civil liability such as cessation of infringement, removal of obstruction, elimination of danger, and making an apology, the People's Court may support such request.
Where an operator uses standard terms, notices, statements, in-store announcements, or other means to exclude or limit consumers' rights, reduce or exempt the operator's liabilities, or increase consumers' obligations, and the plaintiff claims that such provisions are unfair or unreasonable to consumers and requests a declaration of invalidity, the People's Court may support such claim.

After the judgment in a consumer civil public interest lawsuit case takes effect, the People's Court shall, within ten days, notify the relevant administrative department in writing and may issue judicial suggestions.

After the judgment in a consumer civil public interest lawsuit becomes legally effective, if other organs or social organizations that otherwise have standing to sue file another consumer civil public interest lawsuit with respect to the same tortious act, the People's Court shall not accept it.

Where facts have been confirmed by an effective judgment in a consumer civil public interest lawsuit, in a lawsuit initiated by a consumer who has suffered damage from the same tortious act under Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, neither the plaintiff nor the defendant needs to provide evidence to prove such facts, unless the party disputes such facts and has sufficient contrary evidence to overturn them.
Where an effective judgment in a consumer civil public interest lawsuit finds that the operator has engaged in illegal conduct, in a lawsuit initiated by a consumer who has suffered damage from the same tortious act under Article 119 of the Civil Procedure Law, if the plaintiff claims to apply such finding, the People's Court may support it, unless the defendant has sufficient contrary evidence to overturn it. If the defendant claims to directly apply a finding favorable to it, the People's Court shall not support it, and the defendant shall still bear the corresponding burden of proof.

If the plaintiff incurs reasonable expenses for taking preventive and remedial measures to cease infringement, remove obstruction, or eliminate danger, and requests the defendant to bear such expenses, the People's Court may support such request.

The People's Court may, based on the actual circumstances, support the plaintiff's claim for the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff and its litigation agent for investigation and evidence collection of the tortious act, the costs of expert evaluation, and reasonable attorney's fees to an appropriate extent.

This Interpretation shall come into force on May 1, 2016.
For first-instance cases newly accepted by the People's Court after the effective date of this Interpretation, this Interpretation shall apply.
For first-instance or second-instance cases that have been accepted before the effective date of this Interpretation but have not yet been concluded after its effective date, as well as cases that have been finally adjudicated before the effective date of this Interpretation but for which the parties apply for a retrial or which are decided to be retried under the trial supervision procedure after the effective date, this Interpretation shall not apply.
